scope: Full daily Power Stack research refresh across all tracked categories and existing ideas; US, Hong Kong/China and Malaysia opportunity screen. Research/content only; no site code, UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.
verdict: No existing idea warrants a formal conviction upgrade or downgrade today. The main incremental development is a fresh China AI financing signal: Alibaba's US$10.2bn Hong Kong placement explicitly funds full-stack AI capacity, reinforcing the regional compute/power/cooling/grid demand thesis while also confirming that AI infrastructure is increasingly capital-intensive and duration-sensitive.

macro.rates: US long-end yields remain restrictive: Federal Reserve H.15 for Aug 21 shows 10Y 4.69% and 30Y 5.23%; recent market prints reached roughly 4.7%/5.3%. Keep valuation discipline on high-multiple AI, concept nuclear and humanoid names.
macro.energy: Refined products remain the stronger energy bottleneck. US diesel cracks exceeded $100/bbl during the week and distillate inventories remain exceptionally tight; complex refiners retain tactical preference over generic crude beta.
macro.risk: Nasdaq finished the week down about 2.1% and S&P 500 about 1.4%, demonstrating that strong AI/industrial fundamentals are not insulating long-duration equities from the bond shock.
macro.fx: USD/MYR is approximately 4.04 in the latest market feed; no thesis change for Malaysian electrical/data-centre candidates, but imported equipment economics should continue to be monitored.

categoryReview.Power / Grid: Still the highest-quality core. GEV/ETN/PWR hierarchy unchanged; high yields argue against chasing multiples, while ISM electrical/electronic scarcity and data-centre power constraints keep the operating thesis intact.
categoryReview.AI / Data centres: Alibaba's Aug 23 US$10.2bn Hong Kong placement to fund full-stack AI capacity is fresh confirmation that China AI infrastructure spending remains aggressive. This strengthens upstream power/cooling/grid demand but also raises the financing/cash-conversion risk already tracked in the AI financing theme.
categoryReview.Nuclear: No new evidence today changes the preference for profitable nuclear supply-chain/operators over concept-stage developers. Keep BWXT/CEG/CGN Power ahead of speculative SMR/OKLO on risk-adjusted quality.
categoryReview.Uranium / Fuel: Cameco's latest published July industry averages remain $86.38/lb spot and $95.50/lb long-term. CCJ remains the core integrated uranium/Westinghouse exposure, LEU the strategic enrichment scarcity expression, NXE the higher-beta development satellite; no reorder.
categoryReview.Oil & Gas / Refining: Middle-distillate scarcity remains exceptional. Preserve tactical preference for complex refiners such as VLO/MPC and selective integrated/refining hybrids rather than treating high crude alone as the signal.
categoryReview.Metals: Copper/electrical input scarcity remains supported by ISM. Aluminium physical tightness remains a valid developing theme, but do not extrapolate squeezed inventory signals mechanically into permanent margins.
categoryReview.Robotics / Automation: No commercialization-wave change: fixed/warehouse automation first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, constrained industrial humanoids third, open-world/general-purpose robots last. Current evidence still favours profitable picks-and-shovels, machine vision and industrial automation over humanoid OEM chasing.
categoryReview.Water / Cooling: No reorder. ECL/MOD/XYL remain preferred differentiated exposures; data-centre power growth continues to reinforce cooling/water infrastructure demand.
categoryReview.Agriculture / Resources: Fertiliser and ammonia-logistics scarcity themes remain valid. No additional candidate clears the quality/relevance bar today beyond the existing CF/UAN/CHE.UN/NVGS/Vopak research queue.

newOpportunitySearch.US: No new US name clears the promotion bar today; existing ROK/NVGS/CF/MWA/AA-CENX research queue remains more differentiated than incremental duplicates.
newOpportunitySearch.HongKongChina: Alibaba (9988.HK/BABA) receives a fresh AI-infrastructure financing watch flag, not promotion: the placement is powerful capex confirmation but the equity is a broad platform exposure and the financing itself highlights capital intensity. Existing state-capex power/grid/nuclear and listed automation exposures remain cleaner Power Stack expressions.
newOpportunitySearch.Malaysia: No new Malaysian ticker clears the bar today. Existing CBHB/Powerwell/MNHLDG and resource candidates remain the priority comparison set; avoid adding another data-centre contractor without superior backlog, margins, balance sheet or customer diversification.
